# How Sansad Showdown stages a special move

Source: ["Sansad Showdown Has Some CRAZY Powers!"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-EqFYKOjTos) (2:11). I stepped through it at roughly one frame every two seconds, 60 frames in all, with auto-captions on.

**What I could and couldn't check.** I can see frames but can't hear audio. The spoken lines below come from YouTube's auto-generated English captions, which are a machine translation of the Hindi speech, so they show *that* a real speech clip plays and roughly what it says, not the exact words. Two-second steps also mean I may have missed very short beats.

---

## The main finding

Each Super plays **one continuous real speech clip, 6–9 seconds long, that runs under the whole sequence**, across every camera cut. The on-screen speech bubbles are a *separate, written* layer: short jokes that echo the clip in two or three beats, timed to the action. So there are three layers at once:

1. **The real voice clip** (the politician's actual speech).
2. **Written speech bubbles** above the characters (the game's own jokes).
3. **Big floating words** in the scene ("GULP!", "BULLDOZER AA GAYA!").

That is why it lands: you hear the real person, read the joke, and watch the thing they said happen.

---

## The six beats (same in every Super)

Timed from "Gaddha Blast" (0:33–0:45, about 10 seconds; the round timer stays frozen at 46 throughout).

| Beat | Time | What happens | On screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Contact | 0:33 | The attacker closes in and grabs or strikes. Normal camera. | Touch controls still visible |
| 2. Title card | 0:35 | A dark band with gold edges sweeps across the middle of the screen. The speech clip starts here. | Fighter name (small), Super name (large italic), face portrait at the right end. A bubble above the attacker: "Gaddha-mukt Bharat… ek minute." |
| 3. The prop arrives | 0:37 | Hard cut to a new angle. A labelled 3D prop appears: a pothole opens under the victim, an "E20" machine drops in. | Floating label "GANNA → E20!". Victim's bubble: "Arey pothole!" |
| 4. Insert shot | 0:39 | Extreme close-up of the prop doing its thing (a stick feeding the machine). | Nothing else; just the prop, large |
| 5. Payoff | 0:41 | Wide shot. Fire erupts from the pothole; the attacker walks away from it without looking back. | Fire lights the scene |
| 6. Punchline | 0:43 | Victim flat on the floor. Camera returns to the fight view. Controls come back at 0:45. | Attacker's bubble: "Quality ka koi compromise nahi!" |

The health bars and timer stay on screen the whole time. Nothing is skippable; it's short enough not to need it.

---

## Other things worth copying as craft

- **The victim always reacts in writing.** A confused one-liner from the person being hit ("where did this bulldozer come from?!") is half the comedy.
- **Props carry labels.** "E20", "ALOO → SONA", "BUDGET 2026". You never have to guess what the object is.
- **Every Super relights the stage**: purple for magic, dim for the time freeze, orange for fire.
- **The crowd holds placards** with slogans for whoever is fighting, and reacts with confetti in the fighter's colour.
- **A closing stamp**: a slanted, full-screen word ("GHEE KHATAM!") as the last frame before play resumes.
- **Their crowd is simple coloured pegs.** The polish is spent on the two fighters, the props and the lighting, not the audience.

---

## What this means for our build

### Our Super template
Six beats, 8–10 seconds, timer frozen:
1. **Contact** in normal play.
2. **Title card** sweeps in; **the real interview clip starts** and runs to the end.
3. **Prop arrives**: hard cut, labelled 3D prop.
4. **Insert shot**: close-up of the prop.
5. **Payoff**: wide shot, stage relit, attacker walks away.
6. **Punchline**: victim down, closing stamp, back to the fight.

Three text layers, as they do it: the real clip (plus our source stamp, e.g. `DEALBOOK · NOV 2023`), written bubbles for both fighters, and big floating words.

This changes one thing in the plan: Super clips need to be **6–9 seconds of continuous speech**, not the under-6-second snippets I suggested. Signature moves keep short clips (1–2 seconds).

### Melon Tusk — "FUNDING SECURED"
- **Clip:** the DealBook answer to advertisers ("If somebody's going to try to blackmail me with advertising… go f— yourself… Is that clear?"). It's about the right length and has a built-in rhythm of three hits.
- **Beats:** title card → he pulls out a phone and a giant post card "Funding secured." drops into the stage like a billboard → insert shot of a stock ticker spiking to 420 → a rocket lifts off behind him, flips and lands on the opponent → stage goes red-alert → he walks off.
- **Bubbles:** Tusk: "Considering taking this fight private." / Victim: "Wait, is the funding actually secured?!" / Floating: "$420" "TO THE MOON" / Closing stamp: "SEC SETTLEMENT!"

### Peter Teal — "THE HESITATION"
- **Clip:** the Douthat exchange: "You would prefer the human race to endure, right?" — "Uh…" — "You're hesitating." — "Well, I don't know. I would— I would—". The pause *is* the move.
- **Beats:** title card → a talk-show desk and microphone drop in; the interviewer's question appears as a caption → insert shot: extreme close-up of Teal's face, frozen, a clock ticking → everything in the stage stops except the opponent's health, which drains for as long as the silence lasts → the stage goes grey and still → he finally shrugs.
- **Bubbles:** Victim: "It's a yes or no question!" / Floating: "…" growing larger each second / Closing stamp: "STILL THINKING."

### Checked against the audio (16 Nov 2026)

I downloaded the video's Hindi soundtrack and transcribed it. It confirms the captions and gives real clip lengths:

| Move | Spoken clip | Length |
|---|---|---|
| Gaddha Blast | "Jitna kaam maine das saal mein kiya, woh toh trailer tha… asli film abhi shuru hona baaki hai" | about 12 s |
| Aloo Se Sona | "Aisi machine lagaunga, is side se aloo ghusega, us side se sona niklega" | about 12 s |
| Time Is Money | "Money follows, my brother, money follows…" | about 6 s |
| Rail Raja Express | "Yeh baat sahi nahi hai ki rail maanga gaya hai…" | about 5 s |
| Budget | "Hamara rupaya theek chal raha hai" | about 2 s |
| Manch Chhodo | "Jis raah pe tum chal rahe ho beta, ek din poori tarah phasoge…" | about 6 s |
| Closing stamp | A voice says "Ghee khatam!" | 1 s |

So Super clips run **5–12 seconds**, longer than I first guessed, and the closing stamp is voiced too.
